open_prs.title: enhancements: Messenger gifts - the pre-order and edition bonuses, as…
open_prs.body:
… a switch

The game asks the system which add-ons the account has (sceAppContentGetAddcontInfoList) and files each under its label's last two digits (CSDlcBackingData, event flags 6900+n). The stub answered an empty list, so the pre-order and edition messenger gifts (add-ons 0, 1 and 2: the Stump Messengers' "Accept Gift from Messengers" behind the Hunter's Dream workshop, goods 4900..4902) could never be taken.

A fifth PC enhancement, Messenger gifts, off by default: the setup window's PC Enhancements tab, F10 and the game's System > PC Enhancements (message 124005), world.messenger_gifts in bbhost.toml, BBHOST_MESSENGER_GIFTS. On, the call fills three SceAppContentAddcontInfo records as the game's refresh expects: a null list for the count, then the records. Off, the list stays empty, and the game's own common event 3500 takes the hats back. The Old Hunters (add-on 3) keeps coming from the old-hunters patch's package edition.

Checked: config_test covers the key and the environment switch; the Windows build relinks; in game, with the switch on, the log reports three add-ons at the first query and the Stump Messengers offer the gift menu with the three hats to an existing character, on the US and the JP dump.

open_prs.title: options: mark Frame rate "(requires restart)" in the F10 menu
open_prs.body:
The frame rate is read when the game starts. Its note in the F10 menu says so ("Applies on the next run."), but its row isn't marked "(requires restart)" the way Camera tuning, Shaders and the PC enhancements are, because its `restart` flag was `false`. Changed in game, it looks taken and does nothing.

I ran into this on v0.2.19 (Windows, RTX 5070). In both sessions the rate the game started with held to the end, going by the 300-flip reports:

- started at 60, switched to Uncapped: 60.0 fps until I quit;
- started Uncapped, switched to 60: 100-136 fps until I quit.

The window mode changed at once both times, so it looked as if the settings were applying. That's what made the effects' flicker at high frame rates look random to me: it follows the rate the game started with.

**Change:** `restart = true` on the Frame rate row in `src/host/options.cpp`. The flag is only read to draw that label (the row drawing at line 1336), so nothing else changes. The game's own System > PC Settings > Frame Rate help already says "Applies on the next run." and is untouched.

**Testing:** not built locally, since the Windows executable is cross-compiled from Linux. Once CI has built this PR, I'll check the F10 menu with its Windows build and add a screenshot here.

open_prs.title: net: add Discord Rich Presence for character and area
open_prs.body: # Discord Rich Presence for BBHost - Add an opt-in Discord Rich Presence setting in the BBHost launcher and in-game settings, persisted with BBHost options. - Connect to Discord over local IPC and show launcher, main-menu, loaded-character name and level, and the player's live area. - Read the current world block through BBHost's `world_player_block()` API and debounce area changes to avoid transient transition values. - Match live character level and play time to the save summary so the correct character name is displayed, including after an in-game save switch. - Recover if Discord starts after BBHost or its IPC connection is lost: retry connections with a backoff and periodically republish unchanged activity. Linux socket writes use `MSG_NOSIGNAL` to prevent a closed socket from raising `SIGPIPE`. - Keep engine addresses and save-layout offsets in `include/bbhost/engine/sprj/game_data_man.hpp`, with a compile-time assertion for the validated GameDataMan singleton address. - Include Discord's public `discord_rpc.h` declarations and the upstream MIT license. BBHost supplies its own IPC transport; it does not link the upstream SDK library binary. The configured Discord Application ID, `1562063078466650206`, belongs to my Discord Developer Portal application. Its application name and artwork provide the displayed identity. Maintainers can replace it with a project-owned application if preferred. ## Testing - Manual Windows and Linux Mint testing confirmed the launcher and main-menu states, loaded character name and level, save switching, and live area updates. - Closing Discord during an area transition did not crash the game. After closing Discord, changing areas, and reopening Discord, Rich Presence recovered after approximately 5–6 seconds and showed the correct character, level, and area. Changing saves in-game also updated the character information correctly.(Both tested on Windows 11 and Linux Mint 22.3 x86_64) - Starting Discord well after the game still resulted in the game being detected. Initial `SET_ACTIVITY` write failures appeared in the log until IPC reconnected; the current activity was then published. - Tested areas included DLC regions, and area tracking continued to update across map and save changes. - The build-and-test workflow passed for this commit: [build run 39672114182](https://github.com/ReveKo0o/bbhost/actions/runs/39672114182). - Linux and Windows package builds completed successfully for this commit, including Linux and Steam Deck artifacts: [package run 39671376046](https://github.com/ReveKo0o/bbhost/actions/runs/39671376046). These are Actions artifacts only; no official release was published. ## Known limitations / possible follow-up work - Some blocks do not yet have a friendly area name and appear as a generic label such as `Area 21`; this was observed in parts of Nightmare Frontier. - Boss-fight detection and Chalice Dungeon glyph display are not implemented. - The IPC handshake is synchronous and has no timeout; an unresponsive Discord endpoint could block the calling thread. Moving IPC off the game thread or adding bounded handshake timeouts remains follow-up work. - If a live character cannot be matched unambiguously to a save summary, its name is withheld rather than guessed. ## Notes Supersedes #159

open_prs.title: macos: bbhost on Apple Silicon (Rosetta 2 + MoltenVK), playable at ~30 fps
open_prs.body:
Hi team, this PR adds macOS on Apple Silicon as a third platform.
bbhost is built as an x86_64 program, so Rosetta 2 (Apple's x86-64 to arm64 translator) runs both bbhost and the game's code in one process, as on a PC. Vulkan goes through MoltenVK (Vulkan on top of Metal).
The game is playable: about 28-30 fps at 1080p on my 2021 M1 Pro, with some pop-in the first time an area or an enemy appears.

## What's in it

- **Build:** `tools/build_macos.sh`, an x86_64 build against the LunarG Vulkan SDK, with SDL3 and ffmpeg's movie decoders built static. Targets macOS 15, the first Rosetta that runs AVX/AVX2
- **Address layout:** bbhost is linked at 0x10000 (no PIE) and holds the guest's address windows from the start; the eboot loads at 0x300000000
- **CPU side:** guest TLS as a pthread key read at `gs:[8*key]`, Mach-O assembly (`ASM_SYM`), macOS signal contexts, the futex on `os_sync_wait_on_address`, 8 MiB stacks for host threads that run guest callbacks, an AVX check at start, masked stores rewritten so they only write their selected bytes under Rosetta, precise host sleeps
- **GPU side:** MoltenVK's gaps covered behind device features or a runtime `g.moltenvk` check (vertex lane without subgroup built-ins, rect lists through tessellation, R32G32B32 textures, D24S8, mirror clamp, Metal's per-stage limits and buffer slots, device-address memory lifetimes)
- **Performance on MoltenVK:** NoContraction dropped (MoltenVK turns each decorated op into an unoptimised helper: the clinic went from 128 to ~35 ms a frame), SFX particles as one vertex stage, clear folding, new pipelines built on workers, 8 command buffers in flight. Each has a switch, listed in `docs/rendering.md` § MoltenVK defaults
- **Packaging and CI:** a signed (ad hoc) zip with its own Vulkan loader and MoltenVK, macOS assets for the updater and the plugins, `tests-macos` and `package-macos` jobs
- **Docs:** README, building, running, rendering, and the macOS rules CI can't catch in CONTRIBUTING

## Changes to shared code (Linux/Windows)

Most of the port is behind `__APPLE__` (macOS system code) or a runtime `g.moltenvk` check (MoltenVK only), so Linux and Windows don't run it.
A few changes do reach Linux/Windows. Each one is there for a reason: either it fixes a real bug that MoltenVK made visible (desktop drivers happened to tolerate it), or it depends on what the GPU supports, not on the OS.

How they were kept safe:

- every hunk touching shared code was reviewed and sorted: macOS/MoltenVK only, behind a device feature, or unconditional. Only the last two are listed below
- device features over platform checks: a GPU that has the format or feature takes exactly the same path as before
- when a path couldn't be tested on another driver, it stays MoltenVK only (e.g. the per-stage descriptor layouts: other drivers keep today's layouts and just log a line if they're over their limits)
- Linux and Windows were built with upstream's own scripts (`tools/ci_build.sh`, `tools/ci_windows.sh`) in containers, Linux at every commit of the series, with its tests (the GPU tests skip there, no GPU)
- what I couldn't do: run them on an AMD, NVIDIA or Intel GPU

**Bug fixes that apply on every driver**

- **gcn: buffer writes outside their V#'s records are dropped, as on the hardware:** this was a crash in the clinic. GPU particle writes went up to 4 GiB past their buffer, into the game's heaps. GCN drops such a store, so now we do too. The check is never stricter than the hardware's, loads are unchanged, and no old cached translation is reused (the cache is keyed on the translator's sources)
- **gcn: a GDS counter's value comes back from the lane that took it:** `ds_append`/`ds_consume` assumed two subgroup operations pick the same lane. They don't on MoltenVK when lane 0 is inactive. It now uses the first active lane and a shuffle, which other wave operations already use. Count and word unchanged; covered by `gcn_sampling_test`'s GDS cases
- **gpu: mirror-clamp samplers as a feature:** these samplers were invalid on every driver, because the feature was never enabled. It's now enabled where the device has it (every desktop driver bbhost runs on); elsewhere they become a mirrored repeat, with a log line
- **render: a vertex stage without a position discards rasterization:** nothing defined is rasterized without a position anyway. Only pipelines built whole are affected; pipeline libraries (the desktop default) are unchanged
- **the pipeline cache's exit save** keeps pipelines created while it serializes out of the main cache, so the cache doesn't change under it (they're built again next run)

**Only where the GPU lacks a feature (unchanged where it has it)**

- **render: 16-bit depth with stencil in D32S8 where D24S8 is missing:** AMD has no D24S8 target, so creating such an image used to fail there. Covered by a self-test that fills such a target before any draw (`BBHOST_RT_REFILL_TEST=1`), run on MoltenVK where the path is live. **Never seen in a real draw**: the game doesn't use that format on the Mac
- **textures: R32G32B32 as R32G32B32A32 where the device can't sample it:** such a device used to get an out-of-spec image that failed. Devices that can sample it are unchanged

**Same behaviour, different code**

- **occlusion:** one item buffer and one result buffer, a slice per command-buffer slot, instead of one of each per slot. Same sizes, memory types and offsets. Fewer buffers for a driver to keep resident is no worse anywhere
- **core: host_exe_path on every platform:** same system calls as before (`/proc/self/exe` on Linux, `GetModuleFileName` on Windows)
- a T# with no base is logged as a null texture instead of an unsupported format (message only)
- **release.yml:** the macOS assets go through a step of their own that is allowed to fail, so a bad Mac package can't block the Linux/Windows release

**One-off for every user**

- the translator's fingerprint changed, meaning **every user rebuilds their shader cache once** (a slow first boot after the update)

## How it was tested

- **macOS:** ctest 60/60 (pass or skip), `bbhost --stream-selftest` (also with the validation layer), the release zip run on its own with no environment variables
- **In game:** from the clinic to Central Yharnam, the sewers, Father Gascoigne, Hemwick, the Fishing Hamlet, the Nightmare Frontier and the Forbidden Woods. Online was briefly tried
- **Linux:** `tools/ci_build.sh` in an `ubuntu:24.04` container: builds, 59/59 pass or skip. It also builds at every commit of the series
- **Windows:** `tools/ci_windows.sh` (release build) in an `archlinux` container: bbhost.exe, the plugins and the zip build

## Tested only on

- one M1 Pro (16 GB) on macOS 27.0, Apple clang with the macOS 27 SDK
- MoltenVK 1.4.2 from the LunarG SDK 1.4.363.0
- not tried: other Apple chips, 8 GB Macs, Intel Macs, co-op, plugins on the Mac

## Notes

- This is based on master `566184a`, like the render stack (#148 to #156). Both change the same files (`render.cpp`, `gpu.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt` and ~40 others), so whichever lands second needs a big rebase. Which order do you prefer?
- Written with Claude Code: every commit has a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer
- Once `tests-macos` and `package-macos` have passed on the runners for a while, they can become required checks (the comments at the top of the workflows say how)

open_prs.title: perf/flip-timeline after #139: command processor 82 -> 121 fps in a CPU-bound area, compute buffers, shader trims (CI build)
open_prs.body:
Kyo's commits on `perf/flip-timeline` after the 22 that #139 took from #135 (`799871b..90ca92b`, 22 commits), for a CI build. #135 was closed in favour of #139; this does not replace it.

**Note for #139:** these sit on master `566184a`, not on `perf/next`. Cherry-picked onto `perf/next` they conflict first at `19319ed` (`src/engine/frame_rate.cpp`), and `5748747` (NVIDIA presenter copy on its own queue) goes against #139's choice to keep NVIDIA's copy in the stream.

## Today's results (Radeon 8060S, Kyo's hall, headless 1080p unless stated)

**Command processor** (it was the limit, `bb-cp0` at 100%, GPU 70-75% busy):
- `9a2cb17`: an indexed draw's last vertex (`2921fbe`'s flicker fix) was worked out for every vertex record by scanning every index. It was 20.5% of the command processor; now it's worked out only for records a snapshot may take. **82-86 → 116 fps.**
- `57e0710`: the counters beside the constant-buffer and vertex snapshots no longer use locked adds. One right after each copy into the write-combined ring waited for the copy to drain: 8.6% of the command processor. With both, the hall runs **GPU-bound at 121-124 fps** (GPU 98%, CP 90-92%).
- `90ca92b`: a target's write time read once a flip, not at every write (2.3% of the CP at 360p).
- At 360p, where the CP is still the limit: ~186 fps; a draw costs ~4.5 µs of CP, down from ~9.4.

**Compute** (`c0241e7`): compute shaders' constant buffers, tables and typed loads read through pushed storage buffers instead of the page table. `2da7fe60`: 36,677 → 22,594 instructions, 251 → 207 VGPRs, **0.55 → 0.43 ms a frame**; all compute 0.96 → 0.81 ms. Every dispatch in a run bound. `BBHOST_CS_BUFFERS=0` reverts.

**Shaders** (`ca630a4`, `d39e5d3`, `db76b22`, `fe25796`): rsq/rcp clamp as bit ops, legacy-multiply select form on AMD drivers, packed vertex attributes, constant buffers pushed at their exact base. They cut instruction counts, but GPU time in the hall didn't change measurably. Each has its own `BBHOST_*` switch.

**Also:** `2921fbe` (sfx/vfx flicker fix), `7fc8ab0` (lift: `execz` regions as real branches), `2ac3378` (the lift test for the packed loader, which failed CI on `c0241e7`).

Not tested on NVIDIA.

open_prs.title: gx trace: emit records the command processor never takes go after 600 flips
open_prs.body:
## What

`gx_hook` stores an `EmitRec` (about 2 KiB with its `GxRec`) in `g_by_packet` for every GX command emitter call, keyed by the command buffer's write pointer. Only `take_record` removes one - when a draw or dispatch the command processor executes looks that packet up. Records whose packets are never looked up stay until the map passes 2^20 entries and is cleared.

In play that is about three records a frame: **~20 MiB of process memory a minute at 60 FPS (~12 MiB at 30), up to ~2 GiB before the clear.** The GX backend is the default renderer, so every platform has it.

## Fix

A FIFO of (write pointer, flip) per emit. A record still in the map 600 flips after its emit is dropped, unless that write pointer was emitted again since (the newer record keeps a newer flip). The command processor runs at most `BBHOST_CP_BACKLOG` (10) submits behind, so a record that old can no longer be taken. The size check stays as a backstop.

## How it was found and checked

On Windows (MSYS2 clang), on a local branch based on c421ea0 whose `gx_trace.cpp` matches master in this path:

- Every soak grew 14-22 MiB/min of private memory. Ruled out by A/B: RTSS's Vulkan layer, the iGPU's Vulkan driver, `BBHOST_DECOMP=0`; the game's own malloc/new heap stayed flat. The growth scaled with the frame rate.
- A malloc/operator-new wrapper keyed by immediate caller (a separate diagnostic build) put 99% of the live growth on `g_by_packet`'s node allocation: 2048-byte nodes, 127,381 live of 127,473 made after 11 minutes, each holding a write pointer into the command arena, the emitter's return address and the flip.
- With the fix: committed memory 0.0 and 0.1 MiB/min against 20.7 without it (interleaved 10-minute soaks), and 7,231 -> 7,235 MiB over a 40-minute soak at 60 fps. Twelve area-check places, before vs after, two rounds each: fps and frame dumps equal within noise.
- This branch (master 566184a + the commit) builds with `tools/win_build_msys2.sh`. Not run in game on master itself.

open_prs.title: Add DLSS/FSR upscaling, paced frame generation, motion vectors and Reflex
open_prs.body:
Add DLSS/FSR reconstruction, paced frame generation, animated-mesh motion and native Vulkan NVIDIA Reflex. Reconstruction runs before the output-resolution HUD; F10 and game-menu mouse coordinates use the output space.

## Behavior

- Setup and F10 select reconstruction/generation providers, quality presets, custom output dimensions, object motion and Reflex Off/On/On + Boost. Temporal changes apply after restart; unsupported devices retain ordinary pacing.
- DLSS supports DLAA/Super Resolution and Off/2x/3x/4x generation. Higher factors are normal selectable choices without an experimental opt-in; saved 3x/4x choices are preserved. NVIDIA capability negotiation still applies, with fallback when the requested factor is unsupported.
- FSR 3.1.5 reconstruction and analytical FSR 3.1.6 generation support independent Vulkan adapters, mixed providers and reconstruction disabled. FSR generation offers Off/2x and does not require NGX.
- Optional FSR 4 source-v07 INT8/DOT4 reconstruction uses separately installed, verified model/shader assets. Missing assets/features fall back once to FSR 3. This remains experimental reconstruction, not FSR 4.1.1 or ML generation.

Three leased output sets separate evaluation from presentation. GPU timestamps estimate source cadence; bounded phase filtering and adaptive launch budgets maintain generated-to-real spacing below the selected source cap. Expired positions are skipped under backpressure, and compositor retirement protects images before reuse. Generation preserves simulation speed.

Reflex uses `VK_NV_low_latency2` revision 3, timeline sleep before input, immutable simulation IDs and submit/present markers. A narrow WSI guard orders sleep/timing queries with acquire/present. The NGX bridge supplies documented Vulkan transfer callbacks to order overlapping fills and image transfers on the evaluation command buffer.

FSR receives HUD-free color, depth and camera/object motion, then restores current HUD pixels. Individually drawn meshes retain object motion; instanced batches use camera motion until persistent instance identity is available. This avoids pairing unrelated foliage instances after culling changes batch order. Optional guide captures retain matching depth/motion/color metadata through output retirement; normal gameplay allocates no diagnostic snapshots.

Rebased onto upstream master `566184a74f071166299bb656c4af479e5bbe2771`, preserving upstream frame timing, native shader lifting/tessellation, particle counters, indirect guards and GPU retirement. Instrumented object-motion meshes retain translated shaders until the native lifter supports their history output.

The FSR provider now tags transient descriptor/constant allocations before preparation and retires them through the GPU-completed frame watermark. Context rebuilds drain outstanding submissions; failed/unsubmitted recordings cannot advance retirement. A fixture verifies retirement before context destruction, without changing existing dispatch-structure ABI.

## Validation

RTX 5080, driver 617.14, one 119.88 Hz display, layered DXGI and an otherwise idle GPU. No driver FPS limit was installed. Timing windows exclude startup, captures and deliberate menu interactions. Tests use copied profiles/saves in Central Yharnam and Hunter's Dream.

- At a 30 FPS source cap, DLSS 3x measures 89.77 display changes/s, p99 13.536 ms; DLSS 4x measures 119.79, p99 10.610 ms. Their windows contain 8 and 6 missing display-timing rows respectively. These are functioning-factor measurements on one device, not a claim of perfect pacing.
- The final executable loads a saved 4x setting without `BBHOST_DLSS_FG` or an experimental opt-in. It exits normally after 189 seconds and reports 3,900 real / 11,691 generated frames with zero evaluation failures. Its measured window gives 119.69 display changes/s, p99 10.784 ms, with 9 missing rows.
- FSR 2x at a 30 FPS source cap measures 59.80 display changes/s, p99 18.964 ms, with no missing rows.
- The FSR lifetime negative control retains 539 descriptor / 207 constant allocations and fails. The repair retires 68 / 26 allocations to zero while pixel/reset/resize checks pass.
- The repaired FSR soak exits normally after 579 seconds. Nine settled samples spanning four minutes range from 8,231.840 to 8,239.184 MiB private bytes (slope −1.540 MiB/min); global VRAM stays around 6.9 GB. The last report contains 31,777 generated frames and zero evaluation failures. Display cadence over seconds 300–550 is 118.24/s, p99 13.362 ms, with no missing rows.
- All 13 native Windows checks pass, including provider lifetime/pixels/resize, motion reprojection, timing/history/layout, shader instrumentation and NGX transfer contracts. Native startup smoke reaches flip 1800 and exits normally without core dumps or unbound imports.
- Final FSR Vulkan-validation gameplay exits normally. Its later F12 capture contains 602 textures and 32,768 events: zero size/clipping, lost-clear, stale-upload or CP-stale findings; all 46 float targets are finite. An earlier loading-containing capture had stale-upload-pattern findings and is not counted as a clean scene result. No synchronization hazards or descriptor-pool/free-memory-in-use errors were found in final logs.
- [Linux build/CTest passes on the current renderer head](https://github.com/FIocker/bbhost/actions/runs/38233840303) `539d45f41e1692379a130d69ff79dca3a900513d` (62 registered cases; hosted GPU/game-file cases skip).

Methods, exact source/executable boundaries and numeric evidence are in [upstream integration validation](https://github.com/FIocker/bbhost/blob/render/dlss-sr-framegen-pipeline/docs/upstream-rebase-validation-2026-10-12.md). Earlier source-version pacing/guide measurements are retained in [stability validation](https://github.com/FIocker/bbhost/blob/render/dlss-sr-framegen-pipeline/docs/fg-stability-validation.md) and [Reflex validation](https://github.com/FIocker/bbhost/blob/render/dlss-sr-framegen-pipeline/docs/reflex-validation.md). Setup/provider details are in [FSR usage](https://github.com/FIocker/bbhost/blob/render/dlss-sr-framegen-pipeline/docs/fsr.md) and [Reflex usage](https://github.com/FIocker/bbhost/blob/render/dlss-sr-framegen-pipeline/docs/reflex.md).

## Remaining limits

The inherited driver profile forces V-Sync off; these tests do not establish a driver-V-Sync-on policy, per-frame VRR scanout or a monitor's low-framerate-compensation threshold. Display changes are not input-to-photon measurements. Higher factors are selectable for broader testing; their pacing is not guaranteed across hardware or displays. Keep 60 FPS simulation for multiplayer.

Fine foliage/disocclusion artifacts can remain with analytical FSR interpolation, and instanced animation has no individual object motion. The repaired soak still contains uneven intervals; finite memory tests do not establish that all allocation paths are leak-free. Existing unused-fragment-output, shadow-depth comparison-format and latency-marker/swapchain thread-layer messages remain. Hosted CI does not replace local GPU/gameplay checks or establish Linux gameplay behavior. Other GPUs, refresh rates and displays remain untested. NVIDIA binaries, game assets, saves and credentials are supplied separately; license notices are retained.

open_prs.title: Stop dispatch trace records growing with tracing disabled
open_prs.body:
Normal gameplay captures compute emitter records even when GX coverage tracing is disabled. The table is keyed by the original guest packet address, while the command processor walks copied command buffers, so dispatch lookups leave these records retained. A stationary scene adds approximately 120 `EmitRec` nodes per second, producing about 14 MiB/minute of private-memory growth.

Dispatch records supply coverage diagnostics only. Capture their snapshots and table entries only inside the requested trace window. Draw records continue to supply the renderer; guest packet emission, dispatch execution and caller telemetry are unchanged.

Original-fix validation (before this rebase):

- Local Windows Clang build and six available CPU checks pass.
- Original Linux build/CTest passed (42 registered cases; GPU/game-file cases skipped without their dependencies).
- Isolated copied-save Central Yharnam runs at a 60 FPS game cap, DLSS Performance and object motion enabled: private-memory slope over seconds 300–900 changes from **+13.681 MiB/min** to **−0.013 MiB/min**. Each window contains 20 samples spanning 9.5 minutes. The fixed range is just 0.285 MiB; startup/loading is excluded.
- A temporary allocation tracker identifies the growing `unordered_map<uint64_t, EmitRec>` nodes. It is excluded from the normal executable used for the comparison.
- The fixed 16-minute run exits normally. Gameplay F12 checks report no size mismatches, lost clears, stale uploads or nonfinite float targets.
- With DLSS 2x generation active, the same settled interval is also flat: **−0.027 MiB/min**, with 20 samples spanning 9.5 minutes and a 0.426 MiB total range. The full run exits normally after 30 minutes; its 24.5-minute settled window has a **−0.165 MiB/min** slope and reports 103,799 generated frames with zero evaluation failures.
- Native startup smoke reaches flip 1800 and exits normally. Paired native Central Yharnam Vulkan-validation runs both exit normally and capture the requested coverage interval. Both retain existing unused-fragment-output, depth-comparison-format and swapchain/latency-marker threading messages; both F12 captures have the same 20 stale-upload-pattern findings, with no size clipping, lost clears, CP-stale findings or nonfinite float targets.

- Hunter's Dream: native baseline/fixed runs and the area transition exit normally and show the same existing validation-warning classes. Transition-containing F12 captures retain stale-upload findings in both runs; neither has clipped larger reads, lost clears, CP-stale findings or nonfinite float targets. A separate 15-minute normal DLSS 2x run exits normally: its 9.5-minute settled window varies by only **0.168 MiB**, with a **+0.002 MiB/min** slope. The last generation report counts 49,797 generated frames and zero evaluation failures.

These measurements address the reproduced steady growth; they do not establish that every allocation path is leak-free. Existing renderer validation findings remain outside this diagnostic-record fix.

## Upstream rebase

Rebased independently onto upstream master `566184a74f071166299bb656c4af479e5bbe2771`; head `0b0ea897469b2efe783cc749b8c5bd9541448502` retains this fix without adding unrelated features. [Current Linux build/CTest passes](https://github.com/FIocker/bbhost/actions/runs/38225507146) (54 registered cases, with GPU/game-file skips).

The integrated Windows executable builds and all 13 available native checks pass; its native startup smoke exits normally at flip 1800 without core dumps or unbound imports. The detailed comparison and transport results above are original-fix evidence and were not repeated as fresh paired tests during this rebase. Hosted CI does not establish Linux gameplay behavior.

open_prs.title: Fix Windows certificate trust in portable curl builds
open_prs.body:
Portable Windows packages using OpenSSL-based libcurl fail to connect to The Hunter's Dream when curl's configured `../etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt` is missing (`CURLE_SSL_CACERT_BADFILE`, 77). Account linking and the game's HTTP requests both used Schannel-specific settings.

Use a shared TLS configuration for both request paths and enable Windows native CA trust when supported by the curl headers. Peer and hostname verification stay enabled; the existing Schannel best-effort revocation behavior is retained. Non-Windows trust locations are unchanged.

Original-fix validation (before this rebase):
- Reproduced error 77 with the packaged OpenSSL curl before the fix.
- HTTPS transport succeeds against both the account origin and the game-service origin using the shared helper.
- Self-signed, expired and wrong-host certificates are still rejected (curl error 60).
- Windows Clang build and seven native regression tests pass.
- Restoring the standard MSYS2 CA bundle also fixes eight existing local packages without altering their features; the rebuilt executable uses native Windows trust.

## Upstream rebase

open_prs.title: Fix chromatic aberration disabling on Windows
open_prs.body:
Turning Chromatic aberration off on Windows leaves visible colour fringing. The Windows copy-hook installer currently returns false, and the copied enable integer is insufficient to remove YEBIS's separate lateral/uniform dispersion.

This installs an absolute jump at the existing byte-verified Bloodborne 1.09 copy site, preserves guest flags, and clears the enable integer and four dispersion coefficients in each freshly rebuilt view before YEBIS records it. Turning the option on leaves the next view's area values intact. Game files and GPARAM entries are not edited. The diagnostic now reads the enable field as an integer.

open_prs.title: present: FIFO where the driver presents through DXGI
open_prs.body:
On hybrid laptops where the display is wired to the integrated GPU, NVIDIA's Vulkan driver presents through DXGI (the log line `the driver presents through DXGI`). There MAILBOX falls to ~5 presents a second once the GPU passes ~60% busy, while the game keeps flipping at 60, and stays there as long as the load does. The same build on the laptop's own panel (native present) holds 60. NVIDIA's *Vulkan/OpenGL present method: Prefer native* cannot help, since the dGPU has no path to that output.

**Change:** with V-Sync on, `choose_present_mode` takes FIFO once the DXGI path has been seen. Only the first swapchain sees `d3d12.dll` load, so the finding is kept and that swapchain is made again once in the new mode (as a resize would make it). `BBHOST_PRESENT_MODE` still wins; V-Sync off is unchanged.

**Evidence** (Ryzen 9 7940HS + RTX 4060 Laptop, NVIDIA 610.88, external 1080p monitor, v0.2.18):

| Mode (75 s A/B, same save, standing still in the Hunter's Dream) | Presents per 5 s after the load | Dropped |
|---|---|---|
| default (MAILBOX) | 212, 25, 33, 50, 162, 300… | 937 |
| `BBHOST_FSR_DIRECT=0` | 213, 26, 37, 72, 271, 300… | 800 |
| `BBHOST_PRESENT_GPU_WAIT=1` | 211, 26, 34, 57, 139, 300… | 969 |
| IMMEDIATE | 208, 25, 37, 75, 271, 300… | 800 |
| **FIFO** | 266, 272, 300… | **6** |

The collapse comes in the ~65%-busy windows right after the load and lifts at ~46%. In normal play (GPU ~64% busy throughout) MAILBOX stayed at ~25 presents per 5 s for minutes.

Played at a 60 cap outdoors in the Hunter's Dream with `BBHOST_PRESENT_MODE=fifo`: 300 presents in every 5 s window at 54–60% GPU busy, 8 drops, all during the load.

**Not verified:** this branch was not built here (no Vulkan/SDL headers on this machine), so the automatic switch itself is untested; the in-game numbers are `BBHOST_PRESENT_MODE=fifo` on v0.2.18, the mode this change selects by itself. Logs available on request (privately — they contain an IP address). No overlap with #100: no shared files, and it test-merges cleanly.

open_prs.title: diagnostics: preserve Windows crash evidence with an external dump collector
open_prs.body:
Windows crash reports can lose the evidence needed to diagnose memory corruption: a downstream exception filter can exit before capture, and a large full dump can exceed the supervisor's timeout before any usable dump is finalized. This adds an opt-in external collector that finalizes a small triage dump first, then attempts readable full memory with a 600-second combined deadline.

Set `BBHOST_FULL_DUMP` to a fresh filename. A hidden helper is prepared before gameplay, with a readiness handshake and restricted inherited handles. Missing helpers, invalid output destinations and existing evidence stop startup. The existing last guest VEH captures before verbose reporting/downstream termination; the unhandled-exception and fatal-abort paths also request capture. Concurrent failures share one capture. Both stages write to exclusive partial files, flush, and rename without replacing old evidence. Triage and full results are logged separately.

The helper is built with bbhost and included in the Windows package. Documentation covers activation, partial files, disk requirements, external watchdog grace, privacy and first-chance/non-atomic snapshot limitations. This does not change external launchers. It is independent of #104 and contains no private memory journal, gameplay harness, game assets, saves or dumps.

Validation:
- Built the actual production collector, helper and Windows crash handlers in a dependency-free CMake project on native Windows, Clang 22.1.8, Release, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`.
- All 19 integration cases passed: early guest capture before a terminating filter, unhandled exception, abort, concurrent requests, clean/forced exits, disabled capture, missing directory/helper, five initial collisions, helper exit, readiness timeout, full timeout preserving triage, triage failure preserving full capture, and final-name collision after startup.
- Tests parse dump directory bounds, saved exception/thread/context and full-memory sentinel bytes, including Unicode/spaced paths. A new native Windows CI job runs them.
- `git diff --check` passes. Full application/release builds and package execution remain for upstream CI; local verification built the extracted production components and handler integration, not the entire application.

The predecessor diagnostic collector recovered two real gameplay crashes (approximately 24–25 GB; 83–296 seconds) and passed a 25.8 GB alias-mapping fixture. These are design provenance, not claims of live gameplay verification for this extracted revision. That evidence led to the FMOD initialization fix in #104.

Implementation and tests prepared with Codex; prior gameplay testing was performed by the user.

open_prs.title: audio: initialize FMOD project language count before failed-load cleanup
open_prs.body:
Failed FMOD project loading can reach language cleanup before the language count has been initialized, allowing cleanup to clear unrelated memory. Initialize that four-byte count to zero before the original EventProjectI constructor; successful loading still replaces it with the actual count.

This is opt-in via `BBHOST_FMOD_PROJECT_INIT=1` while broader gameplay testing continues. It uses the existing SHA/prologue-checked hosted hook and original constructor trampoline, and refuses startup if the requested hook is unavailable. The underlying sound-bank load error is not repaired by this change.

Evidence:
- Two independent Windows crash dumps showed failed-load cleanup using an uninitialized language count; static inspection confirmed the missing constructor initialization and later assignment after fallible loading.
- One subsequent diagnostic-build gameplay run completed without a crash (tester report, window-close log, no exception capture; approximately 101 seconds). That build also contained earlier diagnostics and guards, so this is initial acceptance evidence rather than isolated or long-session proof.
- This PR extracts only the constructor initialization, removing dependencies on the private journal and allocation tracing. No game files, saves, dumps, or assets are included.

Validation:
- Extracted regression test compiled and passed on Windows with Clang, C++17, `-DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror`: exact four-byte initialization before the constructor, argument/return forwarding, reused storage, later count assignment, explicit opt-in.
- Both missing-hook and missing-trampoline modes correctly terminated before startup continued.
- Ten tests passed on the preceding diagnostic build. The extracted upstream test was rerun independently; a full current-master build and Linux verification remain for CI.
- `git diff --check` passes; based on current upstream master `c421ea0`.

Implementation and tests prepared with Codex; gameplay acceptance was performed by the user.

open_prs.title: Optimize rendering and fix Windows stack and effect handling
open_prs.body:
Route texture uploads, carries and GPU detiling through the command recorder. Upload only safely admitted new mip levels while retaining GPU-written contents and whole-source change tracking. Add guarded bitwise depth snapshot copies, immutable compute descriptor reuse, and exact draw state/binding suppression.

Restore Windows stack bounds and HLE nesting across longjmp, and implement the Windows chromatic aberration toggle with protected executable stubs and rollback.

Add regression coverage for descriptor lifetime, texture carry/upload admission, depth-copy bits and fallback, state changes, Windows stack jumps and effect hooks.

Validation: native Windows RelWithDebInfo build; descriptor memo, chromatic aberration and thunk CTests; default and raw fallback stream tests, three rounds each, 1,130 texture checks and 2,919 threaded operations per run, zero differences or Vulkan validation messages.
